Datasets We employ the subset of Alpaca's responses to Beavertails prompts of our FULCRA dataset to train reward models, with 8k pairs of (LLM output, value vector) and labeled harmless preferences. For value alignment with PPO, we utilize 15,328 unique adversarial prompts from the training set of SafeRLHF (Dai et al., 2023) $^4$ . Then, we employ prompts from the testing set of SafeRLHF for harmless evaluation and the helpful-based subset of HH-RLHF $^5$ for helpful evaluation, with 1,523 and 1,177 prompts respectively.

Baselines We conduct value alignment on Alpaca-7B (Taori et al., 2023). Two baselines of standard RLHF method (Ouyang et al., 2022) are compared, using different reward models. (1) RLHF: The typical RLHF method with a DeBERTa-Large reward model trained by minimizing the conventional pairwise loss using the harmless preference labels for the same responses as our value evaluator. (2) RLHF $(5\times)$ : it trains a DeBERTa-Large reward model in the same way but with five times preference data from the same distribution. (3) BaseAlign: this is our proposed value alignment method, applying the DeBERTa-Large evaluator trained with Eq.(1) and Eq.(2) as reward. Implementation details are in Appendix A.3.2.

Evaluation While focusing on value alignment of LLMs, we evaluate both harmlessness and helpfulness aspects. Automatic evaluations include reward scores from an extensive open-sourced reward

model<sup>6</sup> and value distributions computed by our value evaluator. Besides, we introduce GPT-4 and humans to compare the quality of LLM responses.

The basic value evaluator in our proposed paradigm is formulated in Sec 5, which consists of a Transformer-based PLM backbone and a classification or regression head. The model with a classification head is optimized through cross-entropy loss, while that with a regression head is optimized through MSE loss. During the training stage, we split the whole FULCRA dataset into three parts, with $80\%$ as the training set, $10\%$ as the validation set and $10\%$ for testing. We employ multiple

PLM variants of various sizes and architectures as the evaluator. In terms of the encoder-only architecture, we adopt BERT-large-uncased (Devlin et al., 2018), DeBERTa-Large (He et al., 2020) and BART-large (Lewis et al., 2019). For the decoder-only architecture, we consider OPT-1.3b and Llama-2-7b (Touvron et al., 2023). All these models are derived from their checkpoints on huggingface. The training process is complemented on $8^{*}\mathrm{V}100$ (32G). More settings of hyper-parameters are enumerated in Table 2. All experimental results are trained and tested in a single run, with a fixed random seed.

We conduct experiments to verify the generalization of our value evaluator trained on the Alpaca's responses for Beavertails prompts. Two cases are considered: i) responses from other LLMs on the same prompt set; and ii) responses for prompts from other domains. The results are demonstrated in Table 5. We can see that our evaluator shows great generalization across LLMs and prompt domains. This further validates the reliability of the evaluation results in Figure 5.

For both baselines of RLHF (FULCRA) and RLHF (5xFULCRA), we fine-tune a reward model on harmless preferences by minimizing pairwise loss. Implementation details of the reward model are enumerated in Table 6. Then, we utilize the PPO Table 4: Accuracy on all value dimensions of evaluators with a regression head.
